speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Supported the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014, which would prohibit entry and parking fees at the memorial in Campbell while preserving charges for additional services and allowing voluntary donations. Described the memorial's commemorative, educational and archival roles, including its Roll of Honour recording over 102,000 names, before debate was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Eric Hutchinson
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014, which will bar entry and parking fees at the memorial, and described Anzac Centenary Local Grants Program projects across the electorate of Lyons.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014, recounting the memorial's origins under war correspondent Charles Bean and the heavy Australian losses at the Battle of Fromelles in 1916.

speeches.speaker: Sarah Henderson
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014 banning entry and parking fees at the memorial, and detailed local Anzac Centenary grant projects across the electorate of Corangamite.

speeches.speaker: Justine Elliot
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014 banning entry and parking fees at the memorial, and detailed Anzac Centenary grant projects in the electorate of Richmond, including a Gallipoli landing re-enactment expected to draw up to 20000 people.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Laming
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014 and called for a medal to be reinstated for the next of kin of Australians who die in military or peacekeeping service, noting Australia cancelled its Mothers' and Widows' Badge after the Second World War while allied nations still recognise such sacrifice.

speeches.speaker: Fiona Scott
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014, recounting the 1915 Coo-ee March recruiting drive through the electorate of Lindsay, and read supportive statements from local RSL sub-branches on keeping the memorial free to enter.

speeches.speaker: Tony Smith
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill 2014 banning parking fees at the memorial, noting it lists the names of 102000 Australians who died in service and that Senator Ronaldson had championed the policy before the last election.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Australian War Memorial Amendment Bill, thanking colleagues for their contributions and saying free entry and parking should remain so that close to a million Australians can keep visiting the memorial's Roll of Honour and Hall of Memory each year.
